boundary: All rows are learning links and analytical associations, not verified legal or operational dependencies. Original and expanded profiles overlap. No automatic record collection or feedback ingestion.

funding.title: Public finance and funding
funding.lens: government, public money, jobs and enterprise

access.title: Learning and access
access.lens: education, families, culture and public access

rows.name: Pueblo Heritage Museum & Historical Society
rows.question: Can ownership of a building and ownership of its archive differ?
rows.nextEvidence: assets, lease, collection rights, fiscal cost
rows.lesson: A property transfer and collection continuity are separate decisions. Compare a protected lease, subdivision and sale using the same lifecycle scope.

rows.name: Leonardo da Vinci Museum & STEAM Center
rows.question: Why distinguish a rejected incentive from money paid?
rows.nextEvidence: eligibility, lease, audited receipts, actual jobs and visitors
rows.lesson: A project's request, authorization, contract, payment and observed outcomes are separate evidence stages. Earlier ED2602 asked $1,817,044; the revised $885,000 request was $932,044 lower. The September vote rejected that proposal, not every future alternative.

rows.name: Sangre de Cristo Arts Center & galleries
rows.question: Why don't net assets establish spendable operating cash?
rows.nextEvidence: restricted cash, capital obligations, attendance and grants
rows.lesson: Restricted gifts, buildings and endowments cannot automatically cover operating deficits; keep parent and endowment accounts separate.

rows.name: Buell Children’s Museum
rows.question: How can a free school visit create public value?
rows.nextEvidence: cost centers, school visits, subsidized admission
rows.lesson: Measure educational access and learning alongside costs; do not count the parent Arts Center budget twice.

rows.name: El Pueblo History Museum
rows.question: How does archaeology differ from a recreated historical structure?
rows.nextEvidence: site preservation, interpretation, state expenditures
rows.lesson: Interpret the original site alongside historical reproduction and multiple cultural perspectives; state and local funding have distinct scopes.

rows.name: Steelworks Center of the West / Bessemer Historical Society
rows.question: What happens if industrial archives lose their home?
rows.nextEvidence: collection conditions, property obligations, cash flows
rows.lesson: Preserve labor and industrial records independent of parcel transactions; archival conservation has real ongoing costs.

rows.name: Pueblo Railway Museum
rows.question: Why isn't ownership of rolling stock the same as permission to operate it?
rows.nextEvidence: asset inventory, track agreements, actual grant payments
rows.lesson: Equipment title, track access, insurance and safety obligations are distinct.

rows.name: Pueblo Weisbrod Aircraft Museum / Southern Colorado Space Museum
rows.question: Why does an agreement date matter to a museum?
rows.nextEvidence: executed management agreement, amendments, maintenance
rows.lesson: An agreement horizon is a decision trigger, not evidence of a closure or renewal. Distinguish aircraft ownership from hangar tenure.

rows.name: Rosemount Museum
rows.question: Can proceeds from selling an asset sustainably pay recurring bills?
rows.nextEvidence: recurring receipts, asset sale, conservation liabilities
rows.lesson: One-time proceeds and recurring income differ; preservation costs continue across years.

rows.name: InfoZone News Museum / library local history
rows.question: Why can't library-wide expenses be assigned to a single exhibit?
rows.nextEvidence: exhibit status, district cost center, access
rows.lesson: Use scope-specific costs and access evidence before drawing financial conclusions.

rows.name: Colorado Mental Health Institute Museum
rows.question: How can history be preserved while protecting people?
rows.nextEvidence: public collection rights, access rules, interpretation
rows.lesson: Public learning must distinguish historical institutions from identifiable patient records; dignity and lawful consent matter.

rows.name: Hose Company No. 3 Fire Museum
rows.question: Is a restoration grant the same as an annual museum budget?
rows.nextEvidence: grant terms, local match, ownership, maintenance
rows.lesson: Capital grants fund specified work; maintenance and program costs remain distinct.

rows.name: Center for American Values / Home of Heroes
rows.question: Does a large contribution year guarantee sustainable programming?
rows.nextEvidence: unrestricted recurring support, access, program outcomes
rows.lesson: Donor timing and restrictions matter; education outcomes and consent for oral histories deserve separate evidence.

rows.name: Goodnight Barn
rows.question: Why can different historical sources report different construction years?
rows.nextEvidence: historic records, title, structural conditions
rows.lesson: Retain conflicting date evidence and compare original sources rather than choosing the most repeated year.

rows.name: Pueblo Arts Alliance / Creative Corridor / independent galleries
rows.question: Does creative-sector economic activity equal additional City tax receipts?
rows.nextEvidence: study method, local retention, artist income
rows.lesson: Economic contribution is not automatically incremental revenue. Define the geography, period and counterfactual.

rows.name: Performing arts, festivals & cultural organizations
rows.question: How should community performances be compared to museums?
rows.nextEvidence: venue terms, seasonal costs, paid and free participation
rows.lesson: Different missions, event cycles and public access call for comparable criteria without pretending their costs are identical.

rows.name: Pueblo Zoo (related science and culture asset)
rows.question: Which costs continue even when attendance drops?
rows.nextEvidence: care obligations, cash, facility agreement
rows.lesson: Animal welfare and life-support utilities continue; the operator, foundation and public asset owner are distinct.

rows.name: Nature & Wildlife Discovery Center (related science asset)
rows.question: What happens to outdoor education during fire or flood disruption?
rows.nextEvidence: site conditions, rehabilitation obligations, emergency access
rows.lesson: Continuity includes wildlife care, safe access, alternate learning and disaster preparedness.

rows.name: Colorado State Fair & Fiesta Day
rows.question: Do admissions count distinct people or local economic benefit?
rows.nextEvidence: attendance definition, audited fair finances, vendor receipts
rows.lesson: Admissions can include repeat visits; measure fairground costs, retention and youth participation separately.

rows.name: Chile & Frijoles Festival
rows.question: How does a food festival connect agriculture and culture?
rows.nextEvidence: grower and vendor earnings, public costs, visitor scope
rows.lesson: Regional foodways link growers, cooks, artists, vendors and tourism; gross attendance does not measure their net income.

rows.name: Pueblo Arts Alliance & Creative Corridor
rows.question: What does a reported economic contribution measure?
rows.nextEvidence: study methodology, public payments, artist incomes
rows.lesson: Identify the method and base year before comparing a sector estimate with public receipts or jobs.

rows.name: Pueblo Art Guild
rows.question: What is the value of a community gallery in a historic public building?
rows.nextEvidence: facility agreement, program participation, conservation cost
rows.lesson: Separate accessible artist opportunities from ownership, upkeep and rental obligations.

rows.name: Pueblo Municipal Band
rows.question: How can a free concert be evaluated?
rows.nextEvidence: actual award, cost, free attendance
rows.lesson: Access, educational opportunities and community benefit can be measured without ticket revenue; requests are not awards.

rows.name: Steel City Theatre Company
rows.question: What connects youth theater to downtown public value?
rows.nextEvidence: school and youth programming, actual receipts, facility obligations
rows.lesson: Theater participation and affordable access are educational outcomes distinct from venue finances.

rows.name: Impossible Players
rows.question: How does volunteer labor support cultural continuity?
rows.nextEvidence: volunteer hours, operating costs, accessible programming
rows.lesson: Volunteer time is valuable but finite; succession and facility upkeep affect resilience.

rows.name: Pueblo Memorial Hall
rows.question: Why distinguish a venue from its performers?
rows.nextEvidence: operator agreement, facility maintenance, event costs
rows.lesson: A public facility has a lifecycle budget, while each event or organizer has separate revenues and costs.

rows.name: Historic Arkansas Riverwalk
rows.question: How can a public attraction depend on both history and engineering?
rows.nextEvidence: HARP costs, safety, contracts and local spending
rows.lesson: Flood history, public access, commerce and infrastructure maintenance are linked; visitor activity is not a maintenance budget.

rows.name: Pueblo Levee Mural Project
rows.question: What changes if a flood-control asset also supports public art?
rows.nextEvidence: levee safety, mural rights, conservation and artist pay
rows.lesson: Engineering integrity and art stewardship have different duties that must coexist.

rows.name: CSU Pueblo Southern Colorado Ethnic Heritage & Colorado Chicano Movement Archives
rows.question: How do primary archives change understanding of local history?
rows.nextEvidence: collection scope, permitted access, preservation costs
rows.lesson: Multiple community sources reveal experiences that an institutional summary may omit; preserve provenance and rights.

rows.name: El Movimiento Sigue
rows.question: Why is living heritage more than a building?
rows.nextEvidence: program scope, voluntary aggregated participation, funding
rows.lesson: Cultural practices, youth leadership and community organization carry knowledge across generations without implying one group represents everyone.

rows.name: Pueblo Juneteenth Organization
rows.question: What can a community celebration teach about public memory?
rows.nextEvidence: organizer-confirmed events, oral history rights, program support
rows.lesson: Organizers, families and archival sources preserve distinct accounts of freedom and local history; do not infer representation of every resident.

rows.name: Fray Angélico Chávez Chapter & associated heritage groups
rows.question: Why might a property decision affect many heritage groups?
rows.nextEvidence: group agreements, ownership and access conditions
rows.lesson: Shared space, archival access and membership relationships are different from legal tenancy or collection ownership.

rows.name: Pueblo Symphony Association
rows.question: Does a positive annual accounting difference prove available cash?
rows.nextEvidence: restriction and timing, program access, actual public payments
rows.lesson: Revenue minus expenses is not unrestricted cash; evaluate music education and recurring funding separately.

rows.name: Pueblo City-County Library Digital Collections
rows.question: Is a digital collection the same as a complete archive?
rows.nextEvidence: catalog scope, rights, remaining digitization cost
rows.lesson: Digitization improves discovery without proving all holdings are online, legally reusable or independently verified.

rows.name: Slovenian heritage and Saint Mary's Slovenian Society
rows.question: How do immigration and industrial history connect?
rows.nextEvidence: exhibit provenance, rights, community accounts
rows.lesson: An exhibition can connect family traditions, labor and music across organizations without proving common ownership.

rows.name: Dante Alighieri Society of Pueblo
rows.question: Does shared programming establish common ownership?
rows.nextEvidence: program agreements, scholarship payments, organizational finances
rows.lesson: Events and partnership links are distinct from legal control, facility agreements or public subsidy.

legacyLearning.boundary: Reuse dated prior research without silent overwrite. Educational exercises are a separate reader projection.
